regime: 5% global duration shock + Middle East physical energy disruption + AI safety/capex repricing
whatIsNewNow: US 10Y Treasury reached 5.041%, highest since July 2007, with 30Y 5.401% and Fed hike probability ~92.7% ahead of Sep 16 decision.
Saudi Arabia cut European crude shipments after damage to the East-West pipeline and Yanbu loading disruption; buyers are sourcing North Sea, US, Kazakh, Algerian and Guyanese barrels.

The Saudi pipeline repair window is disputed: US Energy Secretary says it could return within days, while market sources have cited several weeks. Treat restart timing as uncertain and a first-order catalyst.

AI safety shifted from commentary into market transmission: AI infrastructure/semiconductor equities sold off, while OpenAI is reportedly coordinating safety work with Anthropic and Google; US political opposition to a moratorium remains strong.
YTLPOWR broke below its prior RM5.65-5.70 first-support zone and closed RM5.51 on Sep 15; HIBISCS strengthened to RM2.41, approaching the prior ~RM2.46 breakout reference.
whatMattersMostNow: Global duration and Fed/BOJ tightening now rival energy as the dominant cross-asset driver.
Physical oil/refined-product rerouting remains acute, but Saudi bypass repair timing creates two-sided headline risk.
AI physical demand remains large, but uninterrupted-capex assumptions now face simultaneous regulatory, financing and valuation stress.
Prefer cash-generative, funded infrastructure and energy-security exposures over pre-revenue or heavily financed theme proxies.

themeRanking.whyNow: US 10Y crossed 5% and global sovereign yields hit multi-year highs immediately before the Fed decision.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: Equity duration, housing, credit, capex hurdle rates, FX and precious metals.
themeRanking.confirmation: 10Y holds above/near 5%, Fed hikes and BOJ remains hawkish.
themeRanking.invalidation: Dovish Fed surprise plus durable long-yield reversal and improving breadth/credit.
themeRanking.nextTest: Sep 16 FOMC decision, dots/press conference and subsequent Treasury reaction.
themeRanking.action: Raise valuation/FCF hurdle; do not chase long-duration theme winners.

themeRanking.whyNow: Saudi cut European cargoes after East-West pipeline/Yanbu disruption while Hormuz remains impaired; alternative crude sourcing is accelerating.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: Crude/products, tanker rates, insurance, freight, inflation, farm inputs and consumer costs.
themeRanking.confirmation: Delayed Saudi repair, low Hormuz traffic, high cracks/freight and continued cargo cancellations.
themeRanking.invalidation: Fast pipeline restart plus normalized Hormuz/product flows.
themeRanking.nextTest: Saudi pipeline restart, Yanbu loadings, Hormuz vessel counts and EIA products.
themeRanking.action: Hold quality energy/shipping; avoid extrapolating permanent $100+ crude.

themeRanking.whyNow: Industry safety warnings are now affecting AI equities while policymakers debate guardrails versus competitive risk; 2026 hyperscaler capex expectations remain near $795B, so cancellation/order evidence is the key distinction.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: Semiconductors, data-centre equipment, power/cooling, software security, AI financing and index concentration.
themeRanking.confirmation: Order cancellations, capex cuts or binding regulation spread beyond valuation compression.
themeRanking.invalidation: No project cancellations, capex guidance holds and funded backlog continues converting to cash.
themeRanking.nextTest: White House AI executive meeting, hyperscaler capex commentary, supplier backlog/cancellations.
themeRanking.action: Keep physical AI stack high quality but separate real orders from narrative; cybersecurity/governance remains selective beneficiary.

themeRanking.whyNow: Physical power equipment demand remains strong, including new US big-tech transformer orders, but 5% yields and AI safety repricing raise the hurdle for crowded multiples.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: Transformers, switchgear, transmission, cooling, generation and utility capex.
themeRanking.confirmation: Backlog/orders and energized MW stay strong with FCF conversion.
themeRanking.invalidation: Funded project cancellations and supplier order deterioration.
themeRanking.nextTest: Supplier orders/backlog and hyperscaler funded-load updates.
themeRanking.action: Prefer pullbacks; funded/energized demand over requested MW.

themeRanking.whyNow: European buyers are actively replacing Saudi barrels while Gulf LNG disruption keeps alternative corridors strategically valuable.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: US LNG, Atlantic crude, tankers, terminals, pipelines and European/Asian energy costs.
themeRanking.confirmation: Long-term US LNG contracting, high feedgas/utilization and persistent alternative crude sourcing.
themeRanking.invalidation: Rapid Gulf normalization and storage recovery.
themeRanking.nextTest: US LNG feedgas/contracts and Gulf export normalization.
themeRanking.action: LNG remains a preferred differentiated energy-security exposure.

themeRanking.whyNow: High energy/freight sustain input inflation, but farm affordability limits uniform pass-through.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: Nitrogen, seed/genetics, crop protection, potash/phosphate, irrigation and machinery.
themeRanking.confirmation: Crop/input ratios improve while fertilizer/seed pricing and volumes hold.
themeRanking.invalidation: Farm margins deteriorate enough to drive broad input deferral.
themeRanking.nextTest: Crop prices, fertilizer/feedstock spreads, farm margins and order commentary.
themeRanking.action: CTVA/BG quality first; nitrogen selective; AGCO remains second-stage recovery.

themeRanking.whyNow: Strategic fuel security remains strong but no new commercial contracting evidence today outranks rates/energy/AI developments.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: Uranium contracting, enrichment, reactor supply chain and long-duration power procurement.
themeRanking.confirmation: New long-term contracts, enrichment awards and funded reactor projects.
themeRanking.invalidation: Contracting weakens or supply normalizes materially.
themeRanking.action: CCJ remains preferred quality exposure; no chase.

themeRanking.whyNow: Structural mine/grid scarcity persists but tariff uncertainty and weak China imports exposed positioning distortion.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: FCX cash flow and electrical-equipment input costs.
themeRanking.confirmation: Physical premiums/inventory draws and grid orders strengthen.
themeRanking.invalidation: Inventory rebuild plus weaker physical demand.
themeRanking.nextTest: LME/SHFE inventories, China premiums and US tariff decision.

themeRanking.whyNow: Gold remains a structural fiscal/geopolitical hedge but 5% nominal yields and tightening expectations pressure tactical performance.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: Bullion, miners, USD and real yields.
themeRanking.confirmation: Gold holds despite Fed tightening or real yields reverse.
themeRanking.invalidation: Persistent real-yield/USD breakout with bullion trend failure.
themeRanking.action: Stage entries; do not chase hedge narrative.

themeRanking.whyNow: Storage deployment remains real while manufacturing/lithium overcapacity keeps commodity economics weak.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: Grid storage integrators versus cell/miner margins.
themeRanking.confirmation: Storage deployment and margins improve while capacity rationalizes.
themeRanking.nextTest: ESS installations, cell pricing and producer FCF.
themeRanking.action: Prefer deployment/integration over generic lithium miners.

themeRanking.whyNow: No new evidence changes the commercialization sequence.
themeRanking.marketTransmission: Factory/warehouse automation, machine vision, motion control and humanoid components.
themeRanking.confirmation: Recurring external deployments and positive unit economics.
themeRanking.nextTest: External production deployments and supplier orders.
themeRanking.action: Fixed/warehouse > cobots/mobile manipulation > industrial humanoids > general-purpose humanoids.
